prompt: A garden bed is L-shaped: start with a rectangle $10$ ft long and $6$ ft wide, then cut away a $4$ ft by $3$ ft rectangle from one corner. What is the area of the remaining L-shaped bed, in square feet?
hint: Find the big rectangle's area, then subtract the piece that was removed.

hints.text: Find the big rectangle's area, then subtract the piece that was removed.
Big rectangle: $10 \times 6 = 60$ sq ft. Removed corner: $4 \times 3 = 12$ sq ft.

explanation: Treat the L as a full rectangle with a bite taken out.
Full rectangle: $10 \times 6 = 60$ sq ft. Bite: $4 \times 3 = 12$ sq ft.

alternativeExplanations.title: Add two pieces instead
steps: You can also slice the L into two rectangles: one $10$ by $3$ ($30$ sq ft) and one $6$ by $3$ ($18$ sq ft).
$30 + 18 = 48$ sq ft ✓ — subtracting a piece and adding pieces always agree, so use whichever cut you see first.
